stages.label: Exposure
stages.description: Eligible thumbnail impression or Shorts feed appearance exposes content to a potential viewer.
stages.caveat: Not unique people; thumbnails in external embeds often do not enter the denominator.

stages.label: Selection or swipe
stages.description: Someone clicks a thumbnail or stays rather than swiping away in a Shorts feed.
stages.caveat: CTR and Shorts stayed-to-watch are not directly comparable; avoid using all views divided by impressions.

stages.label: Watching
stages.description: The viewer watches for a measured duration; engaged views and watch time are distinct from playback starts.
stages.caveat: Raw public views changed definition in August 2026; watch time remains a different unit.

stages.label: Returning
stages.description: A prior channel viewer revisits the channel across sessions.
stages.caveat: New, casual and regular categories depend on lookback windows; they do not predict purchase behavior.

stages.label: Community interaction
stages.description: The person participates through comments, community posts, polls, live chat or recurring viewing.
stages.caveat: Interactions are events, not distinct fans or necessarily positive relationships. Child-directed feature restrictions may apply.

stages.label: Paid support or purchase
stages.description: A qualified user makes an eligible native payment or purchases through an outside seller.
stages.caveat: No universal observable conversion rate from YouTube viewer to buyer, and third-party sales attribution may be incomplete.

metrics.limitations: Eligible YouTube surface, 50% visibility, >1 second; not external clicks.
Official rate only for registered thumbnail impression cohort; no all-view numerator.

metrics.definition: times Short presented in Shorts feed
metrics.limitations: Not unique people, not watch time, not monetized views.

metrics.definition: share of Shorts feed occasions that viewed instead of swiped
metrics.limitations: Not equivalent to thumbnail CTR or paid engagement.

metrics.definition: views which pass the format-specific viewing/engagement threshold
metrics.limitations: Not all raw video playback starts; check report definition.

metrics.definition: estimated total viewing duration of selected content in minutes
metrics.limitations: Can aggregate repeated watches; not deduplicated viewers.

metrics.definition: watched minutes / relevant counted playbacks under report definition
metrics.limitations: Not unique viewer duration or an independent ranking score.

metrics.definition: estimated viewers who had watched the channel previously and watched again
metrics.limitations: Previous history and session window affect counts.

metrics.definition: estimated distinct channel viewers over rolling 28 days
metrics.limitations: Not platform monthly active users or subscriber count.

metrics.definition: viewers identified as first-time or effectively new in the defined period
metrics.limitations: Private browser, deleted watch history and long absence can count as new.

metrics.definition: monthly channel viewers in one to five months of previous year
metrics.limitations: Category defined by watch history; not a personal demographic or inferred loyalty trait.

metrics.definition: monthly channel viewers in more than six months of previous year
metrics.limitations: Behavior segment not a count of subscribers or patrons.
Does not equal unique viewers or confirmed paid supporters.

metrics.definition: terms used before discovering a creator's video via YouTube search
metrics.limitations: Not a full population search-intent census; not publicly available for arbitrary competitors.

metrics.definition: videos leading viewers to creator content through recommendations
metrics.limitations: Not proof of algorithmic rank or complete competitive inventory.

metrics.definition: sites or apps referring permitted video traffic
metrics.limitations: Unknown or unreported traffic remains missing.

metrics.definition: orders attributed to an affiliate or creator-owned store
metrics.limitations: Requires store-side authorization; not computable from YouTube public metrics.

surface_distinctions.measurement: search traffic and terms to an authorized channel
surface_distinctions.caveat: Search results are not a universal channel discovery probability.
An early loyal core can inflate early CTR.

surface_distinctions.discovery_basis: Up Next and other suggested video placements
surface_distinctions.caveat: Competition and viewer preference vary for each impression.

surface_distinctions.discovery_basis: Shorts feed display and swipe choice
surface_distinctions.caveat: Not a thumbnail impression or long-form click-through funnel.

surface_distinctions.measurement: external referral sources in authorized Analytics
surface_distinctions.caveat: May contribute views without counted YouTube thumbnail impressions.

surface_distinctions.discovery_basis: Community Posts on Home, channel, subscription and other supported surfaces
surface_distinctions.caveat: Not available on made-for-kids channels; does not imply paid community.

study_protocol: Define channel cohort, topic, content format, language, period and geography before comparisons.
Distinguish eligible impressions, public starts, engaged watching, unique viewers and payment events.
Compare YouTube Search, Suggested, Home, Shorts and external sources as separate mechanisms.
Sample newcomers and incumbents separately; avoid survivorship bias.
Use creator-authorized Analytics for cohort performance; public counts cannot provide the complete funnel.
Record missing events and non-monetized channels rather than discarding zeros.
Treat interactions as aggregate events; never profile individual children or infer ethnicity or political affiliation.
Pre-register objective outcomes when designing a small content test; do not promise financial results.
research_questions: Which niche has observable unmet search demand in a particular language?
How are impressions distributed among established and newly created channels?
How much time is needed to produce one publishable episode in each format?
What fraction of non-monetized channels remain active after six months?
How does returning viewership relate to monetization once channel selection is controlled?
What independent conversion evidence exists for products or memberships?
